sources.entry: Helium - Floating browser window for macOS.

summary.one_liner: Helium is a floating browser window for macOS that stays above other windows so you can watch media or browse while working.
summary.what_it_does: Helium is a browser window that floats above your other windows, so web content stays visible while you switch tasks. It has a customizable translucency mode that lets you see the content and the windows behind it at the same time. When translucent, the window does not intercept mouse clicks, so you can click, drag, and scroll the windows behind it. The README describes it as a way to watch media and browse the web while staying productive. The README does not describe further features or implementation details.
use_cases: watch video while working in other apps
keep a reference web page visible above other windows
browse the web alongside a document
see content through a translucent window
click and scroll windows behind a floating browser
notable: Floating window that stays above other windows
Click-through when translucent, so mouse input reaches windows behind it
caveats: The README says Helium is no longer maintained
Designed for macOS only, per the listing
